objective: Return a promise for an own-key cache hit or load and safely store a missing dictionary value.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Native async functions and own-property dictionaries are current JavaScript tools.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Cache hits and fill-on-miss are common data-loading behavior.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Distinguishing ownership from truthiness/prototype lookup generalizes to user-keyed records.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: A single bounded key and callback isolate the lesson.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Inherited or prototype-like names can return the wrong cached object or change a dictionary prototype.

defects: Reference/junior and hint used in, while senior used Object.hasOwn: inherited-key semantics disagreed.
Ordinary assignment could invoke the inherited __proto__ setter on a miss under an own-key policy.
Cached undefined/opaque identity, exact loader arguments and failed-entry handling were underspecified.
rationale: Choose and state own-key cache semantics, aligning all boards and hints; this is an explicit clarification of an originally conflicting contract. Use Object.defineProperty with ordinary data flags to store fulfilled values safely, including a literal __proto__ key, without changing prototypes. State extensible plain/null-prototype data records, bounded string keys, opaque nonthenable values, one load(key), exact synchronous/asynchronous failure propagation and no store on failure. Explain average constant-time wrapper/property work and exclusion of loading/waiting. Cases cover inherited-looking/empty names, own undefined and false-like values, functions/Symbols/NaN/-0, null-prototype caches, original failed reasons, preserved other entries/descriptors and a 1000-unit key. Do not claim concurrent miss coalescing.

objective: Separate HTTP status failure from request/JSON parsing failure while preserving the returned body and original thrown reasons.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Fetch response status and body parsing are current Web APIs.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Checking HTTP errors before parsing is everyday request handling.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Separating transport, status and body failures transfers across clients.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: An injected request callback keeps the introductory task deterministic and network-free.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Treating HTTP 404 as rejection or replacing a parse/network reason masks the real failure.

defects: The opening only-rejects-when-no-request wording omitted abort and malformed-request cases.
A fake 204 response with a successful null JSON body could teach an unrealistic empty-body expectation.
Existing checks did not enforce original reasons/body identities, json receiver/arity or parsing failure.
rationale: Retain all three correct response-checking boards. Correct the fetch introduction, distinguish a successful HTTP status from valid JSON, change the null-body fixture to status 200 and add a 204-like rejected parse. Define supplied request/URL, exactly one single-argument call, stable boolean-ok/status record, exactly one zero-argument response.json method call with its receiver only on success, original JSON value/reference and exact sync/rejected reasons. Author O(1) wrapper work excluding request/parsing/wait. Cases cover frozen body identity, request/json throws/rejections with frozen object/Symbol reasons, null/false/zero/empty text, zero parsing for 503 and real status Error/message.

objective: Await a supplied loader inside try so both synchronous throws and promise rejection select an exact fallback value.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Async/await and try/catch remain standard JavaScript constructs.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Loading with a fallback is a practical interface pattern.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Await placement and preserving successful false-like values generalize widely.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: One loader and one opaque fallback keep the lesson focused.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Returning a promise without await inside try lets later rejection bypass that catch.

defects: Senior used Promise construction/catch instead of the explicitly requested async/await/try lesson.
Opaque successful/fallback values, callback arity and immediate fresh Promise return were unspecified.
Cloning a fallback passed the original visible and hidden checks.
rationale: Align senior to return await inside try and keep the correct reference/junior. Bound the loader to an ordinary function returning a native Promise or throwing, called once without arguments. Preserve opaque nonthenable successful and fallback values exactly; a function fallback is a value, not a factory. Explain constant wrapper work excluding load/wait/scheduling. Add undefined/false/empty text, NaN/-0, function/Symbol/frozen object identities, synchronous null throws, false rejection reasons, fallback-not-invoked, callback arity/count and native result return.

objective: Load dependent data only after a user promise fulfills, then build a fresh summary and forward original failures.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Dependent async calls remain standard application code.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Loading posts from a returned user identifier is directly practical.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Data dependency and failure short-circuiting generalize to workflows.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Two callbacks expose sequencing without an unnecessary concurrency abstraction.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Starting dependent work early or replacing failure identity obscures both the cause and request order.

defects: Stable input shape, callback count/arity, zero id, sparse-array length and returned-record freshness were unstated.
An implementation that recreated the original Error with its message passed previous checks.
rationale: Retain the three correct sequential-await variants. Define supplied ordinary callbacks, stable read-only id/name records, zero/large bounded id, Unicode/empty names and read-only arrays up to 1000 including holes. Invoke user once without arguments and posts once with the id only after user fulfillment; skip posts on user failure. Count array.length without scanning contents, return a new plain summary and preserve exact sync/rejected reasons. Author constant wrapper/length-read work excluding callbacks/wait. Cases inspect deferred start and exact arity, zero id, frozen sparse length 1000, fresh result shape, Unicode name and original reasons across all four failure paths.

objective: Build a fresh JSON POST request description, await its supplied request and return every HTTP status without parsing a response body.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: JSON bodies and POST request options remain current Web API practice.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Submitting structured application data is routine client work.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Serialization boundaries, mutable option isolation and status semantics transfer to other wrappers.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: An injected request and bounded JSON data avoid external dependencies.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Shared mutable headers can contaminate a later invocation; error HTTP statuses must not be turned into transport failures here.

defects: Senior shared one mutable headers object across every invocation.
Fresh options/headers and request mutation behavior were unspecified; the new contract explicitly defines independence.
The hint generalized all request bodies as text instead of this JSON-specific body.
Original thrown/rejected reason propagation and serialization bounds were not checked.
rationale: Move senior headers into the call and retain correct reference/junior. State injected request/unchanged URL, ordinary JSON-compatible read-only data excluding custom hooks/cycles/nonfinite numbers, size/depth bounds and standard JSON.stringify. Require exactly two request arguments and fresh plain options/headers with only the authored properties. Return status regardless of ok and never parse a response body; forward exact synchronous/rejected reasons. Explain O(n) serialization/body space in resulting text length, excluding request/wait. Cases mutate first-call headers and inspect second-call independence, exact option/argument shapes and body preservation, trap unwanted ok/json access, preserve original failure identity and literal __proto__ JSON, and serialize a 10000-unit body. Freshness is an explicit strengthened contract rather than a claim that native fetch normally mutates caller headers.
